stem:
The diagram shows Farhan's metal strip. A flame heats one end. Wax marks P, Q, R and S are placed along the strip, with P nearest the flame and S farthest.

Which claim about heat in the strip is correct?

options.text: Heat moves along the strip from the hot end to the colder end, so the wax marks melt from P toward S.
Heat moves along the strip from the colder end to the hot end, so the wax marks melt from S toward P.
Heat stays only under the flame; the wax marks farther along the strip never melt.
All wax marks melt at the same moment because the whole strip is one object.

teacher.key_rationale: When one end is heated, heat moves along the solid strip toward colder parts, so marks nearer the flame melt first.
teacher.figure_note: Metal strip with flame and wax marks P–S.
